chunks: It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, in mursal form, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

Know—may Allah teach you goodness—that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Eternal, and eternity is His attribute by which the intelligent one is led to know that there is nothing before Him and nothing with Him in His everlastingness. By the admission of the common people, the wondrous nature of this attribute has become clear to us: that there is nothing before Allah and nothing with Allah in His abiding. Thus the saying of one who claims that there was something before Him or something with Him is nullified. For if there had been something with Him in His abiding, it would not be permissible that He be its Creator, because it would always have been with Him; so how could He be Creator of that which had always been with Him? And if there had been something before Him, then that thing would have been the first, not this; and the first would have had more right to be the creator of the first.

Then He, Blessed and Exalted, described Himself with names by which He called the creation—when He created them, made them worship Him, and tested them—to call upon Him. So He named Himself All-Hearing, All-Seeing, Powerful, Standing, Speaking, Manifest, Hidden, Subtle, All-Aware, Strong, Mighty, Wise, Knowing, and whatever resembles these names. When the lying deniers saw that among His names, and they had heard us narrate concerning Allah that there is nothing like Him and nothing among the creation in His state, they said: Tell us, if you claim that there is no likeness to Allah and no resemblance to Him, then how have you shared with Him in His Most Beautiful Names so that you have named yourselves by all of them? Surely in that is proof that you are like Him in all His states, or in some of them and not others, since you have gathered these good names. It was said to them: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has obligated the servants with names from among His names despite difference in meanings. That is just as a single name may unite two different meanings. The proof of that is the permissible and widespread speech of people, and it is that by which Allah addressed the creation; He spoke to them in what they understand, so that there would be a proof against them regarding the neglect of what they neglected. A man may be called a dog, a donkey, a bull, sweetness, bitterness, and a lion—yet all of that is contrary to him and his states. The names were not applied according to the meanings upon which they were originally built, because the human being is not a lion nor a dog. So understand that—may Allah have mercy on you.

Allah, Exalted, is only called Knowing not by means of a temporal knowledge through which He came to know things, such that He would rely on it to preserve what is to come of His command, deliberate over what He creates of His creatures, or undo what has passed of what He has annihilated from His creation—so that if that knowledge were not present to Him and were absent from Him, He would be ignorant and weak. Rather, when we see the learned among creation, they are only called knowledgeable because of a temporal knowledge, since before it they were ignorant, and perhaps knowledge of things departs from them and they return to ignorance. Allah is only called Knowing because He is not ignorant of anything. Thus the Creator and the creature share the name of knowing, but the meaning differs, as you have seen.

Our Lord is called All-Hearing, not by means of an aperture within Him by which He hears sound and not by which He sees, just as our own aperture by which we hear does not enable us to see. Rather, He has informed that no sound is hidden from Him. It is not according to the limit by which we are called hearing; we share the name of hearing, but the meaning differs. Likewise with seeing: it is not that He sees through an aperture, as we see through an aperture of ours from which we gain no benefit for anything else. Rather, Allah is All-Seeing, without bearing an object looked upon. We share the name, but the meaning differs.

He is Standing, but not in the sense of being upright and standing on a leg in bodily strain as created things stand. Rather, Standing here means that He is preserving, as when one says, “So-and-so is standing over our affair.” And Allah is “the One standing over every soul for what it has earned.” In people’s speech, standing also means remaining, and it also conveys sufficiency, as when you say to a man, “Take care of the affair of the family of so-and-so,” meaning, suffice them. As for us, one who stands stands upon a leg. Thus we share the name, but we do not share the meaning.

As for the Subtle, it is not in the sense of smallness, thinness, or minuteness; rather, it refers to penetration into things and being beyond being perceived. It is like your saying about a matter, “This matter has become subtle for me,” or, “So-and-so is subtle in his path and speech,” informing you that the intellect has become unable to grasp it, pursuit has failed, and it has become deeply intricate and refined so that imagination cannot perceive it. Thus Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is subtle beyond being apprehended by a limit or bounded by a description. Our subtlety is smallness and littleness; we share the name, but the meaning differs. As for the All-Aware, He is the One from whom nothing departs and nothing escapes—not by way of experience nor by taking lessons from things. With experience and consideration there are two kinds of knowledge, and without them there would be no knowing, because one who is like that would be ignorant. Allah has never ceased to be All-Aware of what He creates. But the one called expert among people is the one who seeks to know out of ignorance and learns. We share the name, but the meaning differs.

As for the Manifest, it is not because He is above things by riding over them, sitting upon them, or mounting their summits. Rather, it is because of His subduing of things, His overcoming them, and His power over them—like when a man says, “I prevailed over my enemies,” or, “Allah granted me victory over my opponent,” which indicates triumph and domination. Thus is Allah’s manifestation over things. Another aspect is that He is manifest to whoever seeks Him, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is the regulator of all that He originated. So what manifest thing is more manifest and clearer than Allah, Blessed and Exalted? For you do not fail to find His workmanship wherever you turn, and within yourself there are traces of Him sufficient for you. The manifest among us is one exposed in himself and known by his limit. We share the name, but not the meaning.

As for the Hidden, it is not in the sense of entering into things by penetrating deep within them. Rather, it refers to His inner encompassing of things in knowledge, preservation, and governance, like one who says, “I came to know his inwardness,” meaning I became informed and knew the concealed secret of him. The hidden among us is that which is absent and concealed within a thing. We share the name, but the meaning differs. As for the Subduer, it is not in the sense of exertion, toil, contrivance, diplomacy, or cunning, as servants overpower one another: the subdued among them may become subduer, and the subduer may become subdued. Rather, with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, all that He created is clothed in humiliation before its Maker and has but little power to resist what He wills for it; not even the blink of an eye passes from it before He says to it, “Be,” and it is. The subduer among us is as I have mentioned and described. We share the name, but the meaning differs.
And thus are all the names, even if we have not gathered all of them. Reflection upon what we have conveyed to you is sufficient. And Allah is your help and our help in our guidance and our success.

key_terms.الظَّاهِرُ: the Manifest; manifest through dominion, clarity of signs, and power over creation
key_terms.اللَّطِيفُ: the Subtle; beyond perception and not to be understood as physical minuteness
key_terms.الْبَاطِنُ: the Hidden; inwardly encompassing things through knowledge, preservation, and governance
key_terms.الْخَبِيرُ: the All-Aware; knowing without experience, trial, or acquired learning
key_terms.الْعَالِمِ: the Knowing; a shared name whose meaning differs completely between Creator and creature
key_terms.الْقِدَمُ: eternity; Allah’s beginningless attribute proving nothing precedes Him
key_terms.بَصِيرًا: All-Seeing; Allah’s seeing without organ, aperture, or dependence on objects
key_terms.سَمِيعًا: All-Hearing; Allah’s hearing without bodily instrument or created faculty

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain that Allah’s names can be shared in wording with creation without implying resemblance to Him?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the eternity of Allah and refutes the idea that anything existed before Him or alongside Him. It clarifies that divine names shared linguistically with creation do not imply likeness, because the realities and meanings of Allah’s attributes are utterly distinct from created qualities. The narration is a foundational theological text on tawhid and the proper understanding of the divine attributes in Shia doctrine.

en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, in a mursal manner, from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following to one of his followers.

“May Allah, bestow up on you knowledge of the good, notice that Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, is eternal. Eternity is that attribute which guides the wise that there was nothing before Him in eternity nor is there anything with Him eternal. That this attribute is a miraculous one has come to light from the acknowledgement of the ‘Ammah (common people) that there is nothing before Allah, with and after Him. At the same time, it invalidates the belief that there was something before or with Him. Had there been something with Him eternal He would not have been the Creator of that thing. If it was with Him how then He could have been its creator? Had there been something before Him then that thing might have been His creator because of its existing earlier.

Allah, the Most Holy, the Exalted, has ascribed certain names to Himself. He told His creatures when He created them, give them the ability to worship Him and made them responsible, to call Him with those names. He called Himself All-hearing, All-seeing, All-powerful, Guarding, Rationalizing, Manifest, Hidden, Subtle, All-aware, Powerful, Majestic, Wise, All-knowing and with such other similar names. When the animosity-mongers, who speak lies heard us mention such names as that there is nothing similar to Him and nothing of the creatures is like Him they began to speak out. “When you (the Imams (a.s.) say that there is nothing like Him and no one is similar to Him then how is it that you also have those beautiful names for yourselves? This is proof that you are similar to Him or in certain conditions and not in other conditions because of having all those beautiful names.” It is said to them that Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, made it necessary for His servants to have certain names from among His names with differences in their meanings. The difference is because one name may have two different meanings. One example is what people consider permissible and is widely used. This is the way Allah has addressed people. He has spoken to them by means of things that they understand so that they will have no excuse in their misdeeds. A man is sometimes called a dog, a bull, sweet, bitter and a loin. All these are different from him and his conditions. The names were not used in their original meaning because man is not a loin or a dog etc. Note this carefully, may Allah grant you blessings.

Allah is called All-knowing. It is other than the created knowledge. With His knowledge of things He knows things and uses it to preserve His future commands and the process of whatever He creates of His creatures, destroys what He destroys of His creatures and without such knowledge He would have been weak and ignorant. We see that people of knowledge among people are called knowledgeable because of the created knowledge, which they did not have at one time. Perhaps such knowledge may go away from them and they become ignorant. Allah is called All-knowing because He is not ignorant of anything. Thus, the Creator and created are both called as having knowledge but the meaning is different as you may have noticed.

Our Lord is called All-hearing but it is not through the perforated piece and with sound so He would hear with it but would not see with it, which is the case with us. We do not see with what we hear but Allah has told us that from Him nothing of the sounds is hidden. His hearing is not in the way we are called as hearing people. We are called as hearing but the meaning is different. In the same way is seeing not that He sees through a hole as we do and can not use it for other uses. Allah sees but not by looking to an object. We also are called as seeing but the meaning is different.

Allah is called Standing but not in the sense of standing in an upright position on the legs as is the case with the things but that He has said He is preserving as in the saying of a man, “standing for our affairs.” Allah stands over every soul and what it gains. The word standing is also in the usage of people. Words like remaining and standing also mean to suffice as in the words as you may say to a man, “Stand up over the affairs of so and so” which means deal with them in a sufficient manner. We stand on our legs, thus, the name is similar but the meaning is different.

The name, Subtle is not in the sense of fastidiousness or being infinitesimal but it is in the rarity and hard to perceive nature of things. As an example it may be said, “It has become very delicate for me and that so and so is very delicate in his manners and dealings.” This means that it is profound for intelligence and difficult to find. It has become bottomless and delicate so much that even imagination is not able to reach it. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, is far Subtle to be comprehended through definitions or be combined in an attribute or in the way we are subtle, small and delicate. Names are the same but different in meaning. The name al-Khabir, meaning All-aware, is for One Who knows all things completely but not by means of experience and learning lessons from the past. Experience and learning from mistakes are of the means of learning for people. Without them there would exist no knowledge. One without experience and learning lessons is an ignorant person. Allah is All-aware eternally of what He has created but well aware and expert among people are those who ask questions and learn. Our names are the same but they, again, are different in meaning.

The name al-Zahir meaning clear and conspicuous is not because of being over and on top of all things or sitting on them at their peak but it is because of His domination and having power over all things. An example of this is when a person says, “I over came my enemies or that Allah gave me victory over my enemies.” In this there is report of the failure and victory. Also there is Allah’s domination over all things. Another example is that His existence is clear for those who want (to know) Him. Nothing is hidden from Him and that He is the guardian of all that He has curved and fashioned. In such case whose existence can be clearer than Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High? You will not live without His creatures, no matter wherever you may be. Only within your own self there is enough of His creation. His existence by far is clearer than ours. He manifest all by His Own-self and is Known by His own self. We are of the same name but the meaning is different.

The name al-Batin, means hidden. This is not in the sense of being inside of things by means of diving or so but is in the sense of His dealing, having knowledge, preserving and regulating the inside of all things. As one may say, “I tried to find the inside to learn and discover the secrets.” Hidden for us is what is unseen and covered. In this case again our names are the same but different in meaning. The name al-Qahir, means subduing. It is not in the sense of plotting, using certain devices and speaking attractive words or cunning means. It is not the way people subdue each other. The victorious among people may become subdued and vice versa. For Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High all the creatures have the garment of weakness on them. Due to the absence of obstacles in what He wills about them, it only takes less than a blinking of the eye to say it Be and it is, comes into existence. Subduing in our case is how I mentioned and explained. Our names are alike but the meaning is different.

Thus, is the case for all the names although we have not mentioned all of them. For learning a lesson what we have mentioned for you is sufficient. May Allah be your and our helper in the matters of guidance and success.”
